title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: Once an expansion decision is made, the system first offloads the draft model weights to host memory.
proves: Nightjar's memory action is draft-WEIGHT offload only, triggered when speculation is already off and free KV blocks stay below a threshold for a sustained period; reclaimed GPU memory is added to the KV pool. The paper frames pressure as 'frequent swaps or request drops' and never mentions preemption.
does_not_prove: Does not reclaim per-request draft KV, lookahead slots, or recurrent scratch; no measurement of preemption counts or recompute cost with spec on vs off.
bearing: C1: narrows the Nightjar novelty threat to weights-only, global; per-request reclaim before preemption stays open.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: must perform an additional prefill pass to reconstruct the missing KV cache states
proves: gamma (including 0) is chosen per batch by a batch-size-context bandit; re-enabling speculation charges C_switch for the draft re-prefilling KV it skipped while disabled. So draft-KV regeneration cost is already modeled.
does_not_prove: Decision is global per batch, not per request; no acceptance- or memory-ranked victim choice; RTX 4090 and A100-40GB with 7B/13B dense targets only.
bearing: C1: prior art on the cost of dropping and rebuilding draft KV (attack: adjacent work); leaves per-request granularity open.

title: vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py (main @9d4192a)
quote: # The request cannot be scheduled. # Preempt the lowest-priority request.
proves: When allocate_slots(request, num_new_tokens, num_lookahead_tokens=self.num_lookahead_tokens) fails, V1 preempts running[-1] (FCFS) or max(priority, arrival); there is no step that first trims other requests' spec/lookahead tokens or draft KV. Spec tokens are only truncated to the token budget, not to memory.
does_not_prove: Code reading only; does not show how often this path fires with spec enabled, nor how many blocks lookahead actually holds.
bearing: C1: confirms the mechanism gap in current vLLM main (supports Open).

title: vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py allocate_slots (main @9d4192a)
quote: Allocate new blocks for tokens to be computed (`new + lookahead`)
proves: Lookahead tokens are allocated per request on every schedule call alongside new tokens (including unverified draft tokens); only verified tokens are cached. Lookahead is bounded by num_spec_tokens, i.e. at most ceil(K/block_size) extra blocks per request.
does_not_prove: For K=3-7 and block size 16 this is at most about one block per request: under 1-5% of KV at 1-2k contexts (my arithmetic, not from the source). Does not cover draft-model KV groups.
bearing: C1 scale attack: lookahead alone is too small to avoid many preemptions on dense models.

title: [Perf][Hybrid] Reserve Mamba speculative-decoding scratch per running request instead of per KV-concurrency slot (vLLM PR 57261)
quote: scratch is not a per-request resident working set
proves: Closed by its own author on 2026-10-16 after a needs-rebase label; no maintainer review or rejection rationale. The PR argues only running requests draft, so at most max_num_seqs scratch copies exist.
does_not_prove: Closure is not evidence the idea is wrong; also not evidence vLLM will fix it. No throughput data.
bearing: C1: the hybrid-scratch over-reservation is a static sizing bug any rebase could fix, which would shrink C1's hybrid memory pool (scoop/simplicity attack).

title: Fix draft KV memory sizing with DP attention (SGLang PR 38811)
quote: this underestimates the draft KV pool and can over-allocate the shared token capacity until startup runs out of memory
proves: SGLang sizes DFlash-family draft KV as a per-token byte term in one shared token capacity with the target KV: draft KV is charged per token for every request's lifetime, not as a separately reclaimable pool.
does_not_prove: Sizing fix only; says nothing about runtime reclaim, retraction, or adaptive spec under pressure.
bearing: C1: confirms draft KV is coupled to target capacity in SGLang (supports Open).

title: RFC: Re-layer Draft SWA into Committed Sidecar KV and Verify Scratch (SGLang issue 35789)
quote: Today, draft SWA is implicitly managed through the draft worker KV pool and coupled to target KV pool sizing.
proves: Open RFC (2026-08-21) proposes separating draft state into content-scoped committed sidecar KV and step-scoped verify scratch, with SWA-only draft memory accounting and radix/HiCache integration.
does_not_prove: An ownership and sizing redesign; does not propose dropping sidecar KV of chosen requests under pressure or compare against retraction.
bearing: C1: adjacent enabler and scoop risk; once draft KV is a separate sidecar, per-request drop-before-retract is a small step.

title: [Roadmap] Adaptive Speculative Decoding Roadmap (SGLang issue 23705)
quote: Load-aware policy: adjust speculative depth based on batch_size/seq_lens.
proves: SGLang can switch spec depth at runtime including step = 0 (spec off), driven by accept length, batch size and seq lens; per-request policy and 'Memory-aware state management/lazy init' are unchecked items; retract is listed only as a CI test target.
does_not_prove: Signals do not include KV pool occupancy or retraction counts; per-request policy not built.
bearing: C1: closest engine competitor is global and load-driven, not memory-driven (Narrow, not Kill).

title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
quote: The core of the draft model in EAGLE-3 is a Transformer decoder layer.
proves: EAGLE-3's drafter is a single decoder layer, so its KV per token is one layer of the target shape: about 1/36 (2.8%) of Qwen3-4B KV and 1/32 (3.1%) of Llama-3.1-8B KV (my arithmetic from layer counts).
does_not_prove: Paper does not state the drafter's KV policy; engine-level overheads (padding, separate block groups) not measured.
bearing: C1 scale/relevance attack: on dense EAGLE-3 targets reclaimable draft KV is about 3%, too small to matter; contrast DFlash 1.14x [L93].

title: Resource-Efficient Speculative Decoding for Long-Context LLM Serving (SpecStream)
quote: It offloads only Target-committed history, keeping candidate rollback local to the GPUs.
proves: Sep 2026 work treats KV growth under constrained GPU memory as the bottleneck for speculative long-context serving and answers with CPU offload of committed KV plus overlapped drafting.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; no preemption study and no separate accounting of draft KV.
bearing: C1: adjacent alternative (offload, not drop); a reviewer will ask why not offload instead of reclaim.

title: Transactional KV Caching for Speculative Decoding under Paged KV Memory (TransKV)
proves: Search snippet only: buffers uncommitted draft KV writes and commits only accepted tokens under paged KV, claiming up to 1.78x branch concurrency on 15-16 GiB GPUs.
bearing: C1 adjacent: makes transient spec KV small; check before claiming lookahead waste is open.

Vicuna 7B/13B/33B on A100 80GB, LMSYS-Chat-1M, CNN/DailyMail, BigCodeBench, synthetic arrivals. Results are reported separately 'For Speculative Decoding' and 'For Chunked Prefill'.
does_not_prove: No numbers in the text; unclear whether the two knobs were evaluated jointly; not peer reviewed; no vLLM adaptive verification baseline.
bearing: C4: direct scoop of the formulation (Kill on novelty of the question).

title: SLOs-Serve: Optimized Serving of Multi-SLO LLMs
quote: Then, the optimal speculation lengths and prefill budget are used to construct batches used in the DP algorithm.
proves: Chooses per-SLO-tier speculation lengths and the prefill token budget together, inside a DP over admitted requests; prefill budget is what remains after decode SLOs are met. 1.76x capacity over vLLM, 1.94x over Sarathi-Serve; SLO-adaptive spec decoding contributes 1.66x in ablation. OPT-7B/13B/30B with OPT-125m draft on 4x A100-40GB; H100 scaling.
does_not_prove: Uses an analytic acceptance model Acc(sl)=(1-a^l)/(1-a) with fixed a, old OPT models, no EAGLE/MTP/DFlash, no per-slot confidence like vLLM adaptive verification.
bearing: C4: Kill. The joint verification/prefill budget under a TTFT/TPOT SLO is published with a working system and baselines.

title: vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/adaptive_verification.py (main @9d4192a)
proves: Adaptive verification already conditions on co-scheduled prefill: verify cost is read from the profiled curve starting at num_non_draft_tokens_total (prefill chunks plus one token per decode), and the draft budget maximizes accepted tokens per ms. The prefill chunk size itself is fixed by the scheduler beforehand.
does_not_prove: Objective has no TTFT term and does not shrink prefill chunks; does not move budget from prefill to verify or back.
bearing: C4: narrows the gap to 'add a TTFT term / let the chunk size move', a one-line objective change (simplicity attack).

title: Optimization and Tuning (vLLM docs, latest)
quote: It batches all pending decode requests before scheduling any prefill operations.
proves: With chunked prefill (default in V1), decodes, which include spec tokens, are scheduled first and prefills get what remains of max_num_batched_tokens; smaller budgets (e.g. 2048) favor ITL, larger favor TTFT; >8192 recommended for throughput.
does_not_prove: Page does not mention speculative tokens; no numbers on how much budget verification takes.
bearing: C4 scale attack: at budgets of 8192+, batch 64 x K=3 verification (about 256 tokens) is a few percent of the budget, so the competition is small except at small budgets.
